analysis.investment_thesis: Elgi makes quality air compressors with genuine global ambitions, but at 42x trailing earnings and 35.6x forward earnings, the market is pricing this industrial manufacturer as if it were a technology platform — and the 12.2% operating margin simply does not support that premium. I do not pay technology valuations for machinery businesses.
key_strengths: Genuine global presence — meaningful revenues from Europe, Australia, and the US give Elgi a rare diversification that most Indian industrials lack, and FII ownership of 22.2% reflects international quality recognition
ROE of 20.1% and ROCE of 21.9% are solid for an equipment manufacturer, showing the business earns decent returns above its cost of capital
Revenue has grown at 10.7% CAGR over 9 years with expanding EBITDA margins — the business is becoming more profitable as scale increases
key_risks: Operating margin of 12.22% is thin for a company trading at 42x earnings — any margin compression from input costs, currency, or competitive pricing would destroy the valuation thesis rapidly
Air compressors face commoditization risk from Chinese manufacturers globally; Elgi's moat in quality may not be durable enough to defend pricing at 42x P/E
OCF was only INR 35 Cr in FY20 on revenues of INR 1,829 Cr — the cash conversion is unreliable, and the FY25 FCF of INR 298 Cr against a INR 17,311 Cr market cap gives a FCF yield of under 2%
red_flags: P/E of 42x for a business with 12.2% operating margins is a significant red flag by any value investing standard — this is an 'extremely overvalued' situation relative to business quality
Net profit jumped to INR 371 Cr in FY23 but declined to INR 312 Cr in FY24 before recovering to INR 350 Cr in FY25 — earnings are not reliably compounding, yet the stock is priced as if they are
D/E of 0.26 with INR 577 Cr total debt against thin margins means any revenue slowdown would stress interest coverage quickly
analysis.detailed_analysis:
I like Elgi's story — a Coimbatore manufacturer that took on Atlas Copco and Ingersoll Rand in their home markets and earned genuine respect. That takes grit and product quality. The global expansion strategy is sensible. But I have a discipline: I do not pay 42 times earnings for a company with 12% operating margins that sells machinery. Good businesses at wonderful prices — that is what I seek. Elgi at 42x is a wonderful ambition at a problematic price.

The FCF yield is under 2%, the margin of safety is essentially zero, and any disappointment in global industrial demand, currency headwinds in Europe, or Chinese competition would reprice this stock severely. The business may well be fine; the stock is not. I would revisit enthusiastically if the price corrected to the 20-25x range, where the quality would be worth paying for. Today, I would not buy.
